content: 1. Nemolizumab suppresses cytokines, which can lead to increased activity of CYP enzymes. This may result in reduced systemic levels of drugs with a narrow therapeutic index that are metabolized by CYP enzymes. Monitor these levels closely after initiating nemolizumab therapy. Adjust dosages as necessary. 2. Nemolizumab decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. 3. Neomycin taken orally reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 4. Nevirapine decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 5. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Nirmatrelvir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by increasing its metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Consider using additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods for the remainder of the cycle. The mechanism is possibly related to ritonavir-induced CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. 8. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by increasing its metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Consider using additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods for the remainder of the cycle. The mechanism is possibly related to ritonavir-induced CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. 9. Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 10. Ofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 11. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of olanzapine by affecting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Otesaconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol through mechanisms involving BCRP inhibition. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or consider reducing their dose. 13. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Paromomycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 15. Penicillin G aqueous decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. There is a risk of oral contraceptive failure. 16. Penicillin VK decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 17. Pentobarbital decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 18. Phenobarbital decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Phenytoin decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Pioglitazone decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Pitolisant decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Pitolisant is a weak inducer of CYP3A4. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for reduced effectiveness if coadministered. 22. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Primidone decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by affecting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of rasagiline by affecting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Limit rasagiline to 5 mg daily when combined with CYP1A2 inhibitors. 27. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Rifabutin decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Romidepsin decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by receptor binding competition. Use caution and monitor. 30. Rifampin decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Rifapentine decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ropinirole by affecting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 34. Rufinamide decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Rufinamide is a weak inducer of CYP3A4 and can decrease the exposure of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates. 35. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 36. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, which is downregulated by infection and inflammation stimuli. Use caution if coadministered with CYP substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. 37. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of selegiline by inhibiting its N-demethylation. Use caution and monitor. 38. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of somapacitan, somatrogon, and somatropin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Oral estrogens may reduce serum IGF-1 response to growth hormone analogs, necessitating higher GH doses. 39. Stiripentol affects CYP3A4 metabolism as both an inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Dosage adjustments may be required. 40. Sulfadiazine, sulfamethoxazole, and sulfisoxazole decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. These interactions apply only to oral forms of hormones and carry a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 41. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. 43. Teriflunomide increases the levels of ethinylestradiol and levonorgestrel through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Tesamorelin decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Consider alternative contraception. 45. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 46. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of theophylline by affecting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 47. Tigecycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 48. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of tizanidine by affecting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects such as hypotension or bradycardia. 50. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 51. Topiramate decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 52. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of triazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing their serum concentrations. 53. Trimethoprim decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 54. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of ursodiol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. 55. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by increasing exposure to BCRP substrates. Monitor for adverse effects and reduce substrate doses as indicated. 56. Valoctocogene roxaparvovec may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity when combined with medications that cause elevated liver enzymes. Monitor closely and consider alternative medications in case of potential drug interactions. 57. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of valproic acid by increasing its elimination. Modify therapy or monitor closely, as this may lead to increased seizure frequency. 58. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 59. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 60. Ethinylestradiol interacts with amitriptyline and amoxapine through an unspecified mechanism. Estrogens and progestins may decrease the effects of tricyclic antidepressants while increasing their plasma concentrations and adverse effects. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 61. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
